deep.reconstruction:
The page has two unrelated layers.

(A) Upper third: a scratch derivation of the one-dimensional continuity equation. Context: the previous page drafts the 1859 cover letter for the Luftwellen paper, and the next page works on Riemann's integration method for that problem.

Consider a slab of a tube or column with cross-section ω between x and x+dx.
- Mass in the slab: ϱ ω dx.
- Let ς be the mass flux per unit area (= ϱu). The written symbol differs slightly from ϱ; the machine transcription conflates them.
- In time ∂t, mass ς ω ∂t enters at x and (ς + ∂ς/∂x dx) ω ∂t leaves at x+dx.
- Net gain is ∂t ς ω − (ς + ∂ς/∂x dx) ω ∂t = −∂ς/∂x dx ω ∂t.
- This equals the increase of the slab's mass, ∂ϱ/∂t ∂t ω ∂x.
- Dividing by ω dx dt gives ∂ϱ/∂t = −∂ς/∂x, the mass-conservation equation in the form used in 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite' (1860).

Beneath this are two fragmentary lines.
- X = ∂V/∂x + (illegible coefficient)·∂ϱ/∂x. This is probably the force or equilibrium relation in a field with potential V and pressure p = φ(ϱ), i.e. a coefficient like φ'(ϱ)/ϱ. This reading is my conjecture.
- ∂ς/∂t + (ω'/ω?)·ς … ± c. Possibly a term arising when the cross-section ω varies (∂(ωϱ)/∂t + ∂(ως)/∂x = 0 gives an extra (ω'/ω)ς). This is also my conjecture; the fragment is too incomplete to be sure.

A small graph sketch (a falling curve with an axis corner) follows without labels.

(B) Remainder: notes for corrections and additions to Riemann's printed papers. Page and line references: S. 6, S. 9, S. 12 Z. 3, S. 14, S. 28, S. 4, S. 6, S. 19 Z. 15. 'Druckfehler' (misprint) appears to be mentioned.

The 'Note zur Einleitung, S. 2' clearly concerns 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines flüssigen gleichartigen Ellipsoides' (1861). It restates how three equations arise from Lagrange's equations of hydrodynamics in Lagrangian variables (a,b,c), of the form
  (vorticity component) = 𝔞 ∂x/∂a + 𝔟 ∂x/∂b + 𝔠 ∂x/∂c, …
where 𝔞, 𝔟, 𝔠 are constants of motion attached to the material element. This is Cauchy's vorticity formula ω = (ω0·∇_a) x divided by density ratio. The note then states the conclusion: if for a given element (a,b,c) the differences (vorticity components) vanish initially, they vanish for that same element throughout the motion. This is the Lagrange–Cauchy theorem on permanence of irrotational motion and the material character of vorticity, as in Helmholtz 1858.

Further notes concern the ellipsoid paper:
- At 'S. 4 (S. 12 Z. 3)': 'and of the ellipsoid not referred to its principal axes, Sx² + S'y² + S''z² + 2Tyz + 2T'zx + 2T''xy = 1'. This is the general centred quadric form used in that paper.
- At 'S. 6, S. 19 Z. 15': the coordinate system may be changed by an arbitrary rotation about an axis, presumably to diagonalize or simplify the form.
- 'S. 14: durch eine beliebige Drehung der Coordinatenaxen' is similar.

No new mathematics is developed in part (B); it is editorial or erratum material.
errors: As written, the flux is denoted by (nearly) the same letter as the density; read literally, '∂ϱ/∂t = −∂ϱ/∂x' would be wrong. With the flux variable ς = ϱu (as the image suggests), the derivation is correct.

The derivation treats ω as constant. If the later line containing ω'/ω is meant to account for a variable cross-section, the earlier balance would need ∂(ως)/∂x rather than ω ∂ς/∂x. This is not an error so much as a different case, and it is unclear from the fragment.

The vorticity-type equation is copied in abbreviated form. A vorticity component must involve mixed derivatives (e.g. ∂u/∂y − ∂v/∂x), so the machine-transcribed '∂u/∂x − ∂v/∂y' is likely a misreading rather than Riemann's error.

results.what: Derivation of 1D continuity equation ∂ϱ/∂t = −∂(ϱu)/∂x by mass balance in a slab
Vorticity components expressed as 𝔞∂x/∂a + 𝔟∂x/∂b + 𝔠∂x/∂c with constant 𝔞,𝔟,𝔠 from Lagrange's equations; vanishing initially implies vanishing forever for the same element
results.modern_name: Cauchy's vorticity formula / Lagrange–Cauchy permanence of irrotationality (Helmholtz vortex theorem)

results.what: Ellipsoid in general position Sx²+S'y²+S''z²+2Tyz+2T'zx+2T''xy=1 and reduction by rotation of axes

deep.surprise_reason: The page combines a textbook continuity-equation derivation with erratum and addition notes for Riemann's own published papers (Luftwellen 1860, fluid ellipsoid 1861). The hydrodynamic content (Cauchy vorticity formula, permanence of irrotationality) appears in the published ellipsoid paper. The page is of minor editorial-historical interest only.

checkable.sympy: x,dx,t,dt,w=symbols('x dx t dt omega',positive=True); rho=Function('rho')(x,t); q=Function('q')(x,t); simplify((q*w*dt-(q+diff(q,x)*dx)*w*dt) - (-diff(q,x)*dx*w*dt))
checkable.asserts: Net inflow into the slab equals −∂q/∂x dx ω dt (should simplify to 0).
For variable cross-section ω(x), conservation gives ∂ϱ/∂t + ∂q/∂x + (ω'/ω) q = 0 (difference simplifies to 0).

checkable.asserts: Rigid rotation check of Cauchy's formula: ζ = ζ0 ∂z/∂c with z = c, so ζ stays 2 (result 0).

transcription_corrections: Lines 2–5: the flux quantity is written with a letter distinct from ϱ (likely ς or q = ϱu). The final line should read ∂ϱ/∂t = −∂ς/∂x, not ∂ϱ/∂t = −∂ϱ/∂x.
Line 2 right: 'ω ϱ v[?] = ∂ϱ/∂x X' is more plausibly 'ω ∂X = ∂²V/∂x² X' or similar; the reading is uncertain.
'S. 6. und S. 9. von Druckfehl[?] erster Fall' — probably refers to misprints (Druckfehler) on pages 6 and 9.
In the Note zur Einleitung, the coefficients on the right are distinct (Fraktur/Greek) constants 𝔞, 𝔟, 𝔠, not the Lagrangian coordinates a, b, c.
The left side should be a vorticity component with mixed derivatives (e.g. ∂u/∂y − ∂v/∂x), not '∂u/∂x − ∂v/∂y'.
'die rechts der Grenze[?] zu bildenden Differenzen' is more likely 'die links der Gleichungen zu bildenden Differenzen' or similar, i.e. the vorticity differences.
'S. 6. S. 19. Z. 15. so darf durch eine beliebige Drehung um die Axe der [c?] ... geändert werden' — the axis letter is illegible.
